method_anchor: Original F plus CROSS_RX50, RDrop1, unified physical Sinc, default main joint head; no satellite; clean only

source_decision_before_target.criterion: Each weakTX outRX feature-margin q10 >= same-seed BASE+.002; eligible feature calls>=99%; weakTX/RX cell coverage>=95%; RXspread/interclassgap <=1.05x BASE; no degenerate features; defaulthead overall>=-.2pp,worstRX>=-.5pp,anyTX>=-1pp. Source only, no retrofit of prior rejected candidates.

adoption: Retain original BASE; adopt neither extra paired RX-conditional mean risk nor upper-half tail risk.
reason: Both weakTX clean recalls, overall accuracy, MacroF1 and worstRX/day decreased versus the same-seed original BASE. Both candidates had already failed fixed source-feature promotion before target access.
goal_remaining: Improve the fixed source-weak transmitters on actual clean target while retaining strong transmitter performance; current negative single-seed experiment does not satisfy this objective.
limitations: One seed each, no sample SD or multi-seed stability claim. No target-based reseeding, hyperparameter search or checkpoint selection.
TAIL minus MEAN is +0.060714 pp overall and +0.223214 pp weak mean for this one seed, but both remain substantially worse than BASE; this does not establish a useful hard-mining effect.
Source outRX geometry uses descriptive centroids with RX exclusion; all sourceRX were seen by the encoder, not unseenRX model validation.
Exposed Phase1 clean benchmark; no fresh blind, Phase2 or satellite deployment claim.
source_interpretation: Observed shallow/middle conditional feature-risk training did not improve final joint160 source weak-class geometry. This is consistent with the failed scientific criterion; a causal explanation for transfer degradation has not been isolated.
